components.css: .ds-header { background: #0b0b12; color: #fff; padding: 10px 16px 12px; font-family: Inter, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-header-row { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; height: 44px; } .ds-wordmark { font-family: 'Plus Jakarta Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 800; font-size: 22px; letter-spacing: -0.02em; } .ds-wordmark span { color: #7c84ff; } .ds-header-cart { position: relative; width: 44px; height: 44px; display: grid; place-items: center; border: 0; border-radius: 12px; background: transparent; color: #fff; cursor: pointer; } .ds-header-cart:hover { background: #16161f; } .ds-cart-badge { position: absolute; top: 4px; right: 4px; min-width: 18px; height: 18px; display: grid; place-items: center; border-radius: 9999px; background: #5b5bf6; color: #fff; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; } .ds-search { display: flex; align-items: center; height: 44px; margin-top: 8px; padding: 0 4px 0 16px; border-radius: 9999px; background: #fff; } .ds-search:focus-within { box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgb(124 132 255 / 0.5); } .ds-search-input { flex: 1; min-width: 0; border: 0; outline: none; background: transparent; font-size: 15px; color: #0b0b12; } .ds-search-go { width: 36px; height: 36px; display: grid; place-items: center; border: 0; border-radius: 9999px; background: #5b5bf6; color: #fff; cursor: pointer; } .ds-search-go:hover { background: #4a45e0; }

narrative.overview:
MobiGo looks like a well-lit counter in a specialist phone shop. The dark Counter Ink frame (header, footer, dark buttons) is the shop itself. Inside it, the catalog is a bright white display case: every phone sits square on a clean background, with its real price tag beside it. There is one action color, Go Indigo, and it only shows where the shopper can go somewhere: buy, add, select, submit. Savings Green is kept for one job only, telling the shopper honestly how much they save.

The system is dense and practical, the way a busy counter is. It is designed first for a 360px phone held in one hand on 4G. Product grids are two columns, shelves scroll sideways with snap, filters slide up as bottom sheets, and the buy bar stays under the thumb. Components feel tactile and thumb-friendly: rounded pill buttons and chips, touch targets of at least 44px, cards that sit flat at rest and lift slightly on hover. Prices set the pace of the page. They use heavy display weights and tabular figures so a row of prices lines up like tags on a shelf.

Layout follows proven Bangladeshi gadget-store patterns that shoppers already know: dark header, sticky search, shelves with filter chips, a variant-aware product page. MobiGo's own identity lives in the details: its color roles, the price typography, and its restraint.
keyCharacteristics: A dark Counter Ink frame around a pure white catalog.
One action color (Go Indigo) and one honesty color (Savings Green).
Pill-shaped buttons and chips, touch targets of at least 44px, built for thumbs.
Prices in heavy Plus Jakarta Sans with tabular figures. Body text in Inter.
Flat at rest. Shadows mean state (hover, floating, sticky), not decoration.
Mobile-first: 360px is the design target and 320px is the test floor.

rules.name: The Go Rule
rules.body: Go Indigo marks only places the shopper can act or the current state. It is never used as decoration, a background wash, or a heading color. If an element can't be pressed or selected, it isn't indigo.

rules.name: The Honest Green Rule
rules.body: Savings Green means "you save money" or "this is done or in stock". Never use it for generic success styling or decoration, so the shopper learns to trust it.

rules.name: The Semantic-Only Rule
rules.body: Components read semantic tokens (bg-primary, text-muted-foreground, bg-save), never raw hex. To re-skin the store, change only the primary-* family.

rules.name: The Price Tag Rule
rules.body: Every price uses font-price (Jakarta with tabular figures) and goes through formatBDT(). Prices are always the heaviest text in their block. A struck regular price is always Label size in Muted Ink, with visually hidden text "Regular price".

rules.name: The Two-Family Rule
rules.body: Jakarta is for headings and numbers. Inter is for everything else. Never add a third family.

rules.name: The 360 Rule
rules.body: Every screen is designed at 360px first and must have no horizontal page scroll at 320px. Desktop is an expansion of the mobile layout.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: A surface gets a shadow only when it floats, sticks, or responds to a pointer. Never stack shadows or use them decoratively.

dos: Do use semantic tokens (bg-primary, text-muted-foreground, bg-save, text-danger-text) in components. Raw palette steps appear only where a badge, chip, or timeline spec names them.
Do keep every interactive target at least 44 × 44px, and design every screen at 360px first.
Do set every price in font-price through formatBDT(), and show savings as an absolute "৳X OFF" SavePill.
Do use Danger Text (#b4232a), not Danger, for any error text, and Counter Ink text on Hot Deal Orange.
Do give every surface a reduced-motion fallback and a skeleton with identical dimensions.
Do pair color with text for every status (savings, stock, errors). Color is never the only signal.
Do register any new custom utility in src/lib/utils.ts so cn() doesn't drop it.
donts: Don't hard-code hex values in components. Re-skin only by changing the primary-* family.
Don't use Go Indigo for decoration, headings, or backgrounds. It marks action and the current state only.
Don't use Savings Green for anything except savings, in-stock, or completed.
Don't put white text on Hot Deal Orange (2.6:1) or Danger text on white (3.9:1).
Don't add shadows to surfaces at rest beyond the Whisper shadow, and never use pure-black shadows.
Don't add a third typeface or set prices in Inter.
Don't stack the bottom nav and the sticky buy bar.
Don't let anything cause horizontal page scroll at 320px.
